★ 27th Annual Latin Grammy Awards · Las Vegas ★

¡VIVA
WILLIE COLÓN!

A special tribute to “El Malo” — live at the Latin Grammys 2026

On Thursday, November 12, 2026, at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, the Latin Recording Academy celebrates the maestro — trombonist, singer, composer, producer and bandleader who pioneered salsa. His longtime musical director Ennio Gatti reunites Willie's original 13-piece band to perform the tribute live, airing at 8 PM ET/PT on Univision, UNIMÁS, Galavisión and ViX.

Willie received the Academy's Lifetime Achievement Award in 2004 and helped bring the Latin Grammys to New York in 2006. For Mark Lopez — percussionist in the Willie Colón Group — this night is personal: the music he has played from the percussion chair takes center stage before the whole world. ¡Que viva la salsa!

The Story

Newark → New York → Orlando

Mark Lopez came up in Newark, New Jersey — Barringer High School, then William Paterson University — in the middle of the New York salsa world, where the percussion chair is not decoration. It's the engine. Bongó, campana and congas set the clave, drive the mambo, and tell the dancers when to turn.

That training put him in the percussion section of the Willie Colón Group — the role he lists first himself — and on bandstands and in studios across the New York scene: the Afro-Latin roots band Rebel Tumbao, the Congahead studio sessions with Raíces Rumberas, and the salsa orchestra Ray Rodriguez y Swing Sabroso. He cut the bongos on Víctor Manuelle's 1996 “Ahora Me Toca a Mi” — his solo sits at 2:25 — and his bongos open the Sex and the City theme. Today he makes his home in Orlando, Florida, and is opening a new chapter: his own band, under new management, and actively booking.

He also helps carry Willie's music forward on the road, promoting and playing the “Willie Forever” official tour — Banda Oficial de Willie Colón: Legal Alien — including the Fillmore Miami Beach date alongside Rey Ruiz, Tony Vega and Roberto Blades.

“Living a spiritual life — with my Lord, enjoying life.”

— Mark, in his own words on his profile. Faith and family sit at the center of the music.

Book the Band

Mark and his band are now under new management and booking festivals, clubs, theaters, private celebrations and studio work — based in Orlando, traveling anywhere the music is wanted.

🎺 Full Salsa Orchestra

The full night: horns, piano, bass, full percussion and coro — salsa dura and the Willie Colón / Fania canon played the way it was written, for festivals, theaters and dance halls.

💃 Club & Dance Night Combo

A tighter combo built for clubs and socials: salsa, merengue and bachata sets that keep the floor full from the first song to the last.

Guest bongó / conga chair with your band or production — the Willie Colón Group percussionist, on your stage, plus percussion features and rumba sets.

Session percussion for recordings (Soundworks, Astoria credit), private lessons and hands-on percussion clinics in the Congahead tradition — bongó, campana and conga technique. Mark teaches: Alfonso Ribeiro (Carlton, The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air) was his student.

Fresh for the Set — 2026 Tropical Chart Watch

What tropical radio is playing now, from Billboard Tropical Airplay reporting (snapshot researched Oct 30, 2026) — the new titles to chart next to sit beside the classics:

Salsa · New Generation

Luis Figueroa — “5 Minutos” & “Como Se Compara”

Top 10 on Billboard Tropical Airplay in Oct 2026; “Como Se Compara” hit No. 1 on the chart dated Nov 1 (6.7M audience impressions, week ending Oct 23). Lead single “5 Minutos” is from El Relevo, nominated for Best Salsa Album at the 27th Latin Grammys.

Bachata · Tropical Song of the Year

Romeo Santos & Prince Royce — “Lokita Por Mí”

Tropical Song of the Year at the 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards (Oct 22, 2026) — and their “Dardos” held No. 1 on Tropical Airplay for seven weeks before trading places with Maluma's “Tu Recuerdo” in July.

Salsa / Merengue Crossovers

Maluma — “Tu Recuerdo” · Arcángel — “Hoy Se Guaya” · Natti Natasha — “Desde Hoy”

All Tropical Airplay No. 1s in 2026: Maluma's second salsa No. 1 from Loco X Volver, Arcángel's merengue chart-topper in June, and Natti Natasha's solo No. 1 “Desde Hoy.” Proof the young crowd still dances to this music.

Also Charting · Oct 2026

Charlie Cruz — “Mi Reina” · Tito Nieves — “Bailemos” · Maluma & Shakira — “Agua”

Current salsa and merengue titles with chart life right now (researched Oct 30, 2026) — Tito Nieves keeps the classic sonero lineage on today's charts, and “Agua” is the merengue crossover to learn next. Custom-order these charts via MR. Music Estudio above.
